claim: For \(0\le a<b<\infty\), \(\lambda>0\), and every nonzero finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \([a,b]\), define \(S_{\lambda,\mu}(z)=\int_{[a,b]}(z+t)^{-\lambda}\,d\mu(t)\) on \(\Omega_a=\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,-a]\), using the principal branch. Set \(\Theta(z)=|\arg(z+a)-\arg(z+b)|\) for \(z\in\Omega_a\). A point \(z\) is a zero of \(S_{\lambda,\mu}\) for some such \(\mu\) if and only if \(\Theta(z)\ge\pi/\lambda\); whenever this holds, a positive measure with at most two atoms realizes the zero. Thus the universal zero locus is empty for \(0<\lambda\le1\), and for \(\lambda=2\) it is the nonreal part of the disk with diameter \([-b,-a]\).

integrity: The proof is analytic and exact; no finite experiment is used as proof.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
limitations: The classification is the union of zeros attainable as the positive measure varies; it is not a zero-set classification for each fixed measure.
The domain is the principal-branch slit plane and the support is a compact interval.
A related 1980 inversion paper was available only at abstract level, leaving a stated literature-comparison risk.

title: Exact angular zero region for generalized Stieltjes transforms of interval-supported measures
